verses.saheeh: By those [angels] who extract with violence
verses.khattab: By those ˹angels˺ stripping out ˹evil souls˺ harshly
verses.jalalayn: ﻿By those that wrest, [by] the angels who wrest the souls of disbelievers, violently;
verses.romanUrdu: Kasam hai un (Farishton) ki jo doob kar khinchte hain

verses.saheeh: And [by] those who remove with ease
verses.khattab: and those pulling out ˹good souls˺ gently
verses.jalalayn: ﻿by those that draw out, [by] the angels who draw out the souls of believers, gently;
verses.romanUrdu: aur aahistagi se (gently) nikaal le jataey hain

verses.saheeh: And [by] those who glide [as if] swimming
verses.khattab: and those gliding ˹through heavens˺ swiftly
verses.jalalayn: ﻿by those that glide serenely, [by] the angels who descend from the heavens with His command, exalted be He;
verses.romanUrdu: Aur (un farishton ki jo qayinaat mein) tezi se tairtey phirtay hain

verses.saheeh: And those who race each other in a race
verses.khattab: and those taking the lead vigorously
verses.jalalayn: ﻿by those that race forward, [by] the angels who race forward to Paradise with the souls of believers;
verses.romanUrdu: phir (hukum baja laane mein) sabqat karte hain

wbw.translation: And those who race each other

verses.saheeh: And those who arrange [each] matter,
verses.khattab: and those conducting affairs ˹obediently˺
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and by those that direct the affair, [by] the angels who direct the affairs of this world, that is to say, they descend with the directions for it [from God] (the response to all of these oath clauses has been omitted, understood to be [something like], la-tub‘athunna yā kuffāra Makka, ‘you shall certainly be resurrected, O disbelievers of Mecca!’, which is also the operator of [the following clause]):
verses.romanUrdu: phir (ehkam-ilahi ke mutabiq) maamlaat ka intizam chalate hain

verses.saheeh: On the Day the blast [of the Horn] will convulse [creation],
verses.khattab: ˹Consider˺ the Day ˹when˺ the quaking Blast will come to pass
verses.jalalayn: ﻿the day when the Tremor quakes, that is to say, the first blast, as a result of which everything will be shaken violently (thus it [the subject] has been described in terms of the effect it produces),
verses.romanUrdu: Jis roz hila marey ga zalzalay ka jhatka

verses.saheeh: There will follow it the subsequent [one].
verses.khattab: followed by a second Blast
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and is followed by the Aftershock, the second blast; between the two [blasts] is a span of forty years (the sentence [tatba‘uhā’l-rādifatu] is a circumstantial qualifier referring to al-rājifa, ‘the Tremor’, in other words, the ‘day’ can [adverbially] accommodate both blasts and other events, and so for this reason it can also properly function as the adverbial qualifier for the Resurrection that will take place after the second [blast]);
verses.romanUrdu: Aur uske pichey ek aur jhatka padega

verses.saheeh: Hearts, that Day, will tremble,
verses.khattab: ˹The deniers’˺ hearts on that Day will be trembling ˹in horror˺
verses.jalalayn: ﻿on that day hearts will be trembling, frightened and anxious,
verses.romanUrdu: Kuch dil hongey jo us roz khauf se kaanp rahey hongey

verses.saheeh: Their eyes humbled.
verses.khattab: with their eyes downcast
verses.jalalayn: ﻿their eyes humbled, abject, because of the terror that they see.
verses.romanUrdu: Nigahein unki sehmi(downcast) hui hogi

verses.saheeh: They are [presently] saying, "Will we indeed be returned to [our] former state [of life]?
verses.khattab: ˹But now˺ they ask ˹mockingly˺, “Will we really be restored to our former state
verses.jalalayn: ﻿They, those of the [mentioned] hearts and eyes, will say, mockingly and in rejection of the Resurrection: ‘Are we indeed (read a-innā pronouncing both hamzas, or by not pronouncing the second, and inserting an alif between them in both cases, and in both instances) being restored as before? Shall we be restored to life after death (al-hāfira is a noun signifying the ‘first part’ of anything, from which is derived the expression raja‘a fī hāfiratihi to mean that so and so ‘returned whence he had come’).
verses.romanUrdu: Yeh log kehte hain “Kya waqai hum palta kar phir wapas laaye jayenge?”

verses.saheeh: Even if we should be decayed bones?
verses.khattab: even after we have been reduced to decayed bones?”
verses.jalalayn: ﻿What! When we have been decayed bones?’ (nakhira: a variant reading has nākhira, ‘decayed and withered’), will we have life again?
verses.romanUrdu: “Kya jab hum khokli boseeda (hollow and rotten) haddiyan ban chuke hongey?”

verses.saheeh: They say, "That, then, would be a losing return."
verses.khattab: Adding, “Then such a return would be a ˹total˺ loss ˹for us˺!”
verses.jalalayn: ﻿They will say, ‘That, return of ours to life, then, if it were true, would be a ruinous return!’.
verses.romanUrdu: Kehne lagey “yeh wapsi to phir badey ghatey(nuksan) ki hogi”

verses.saheeh: Indeed, it will be but one shout,
verses.khattab: But indeed, it will take only one ˹mighty˺ Blast
verses.jalalayn: ﻿God, exalted be He, says: But it, the Aftershock, which will be followed by the Resurrection, will be only a single blast, and so when it is blasted:
verses.romanUrdu: Halaanke yeh bas itna kaam hai ke ek zoar ki daant padegi

verses.saheeh: And suddenly they will be [alert] upon the earth's surface.
verses.khattab: and at once they will be above ground
verses.jalalayn: ﻿behold, then, they, all creatures, will be upon the surface of the earth, alive, after having been dead inside it.
verses.romanUrdu: Aur yakayk yeh khule maidan mein maujood hongey

verses.saheeh: Has there reached you the story of Moses? -
verses.khattab: Has the story of Moses reached you ˹O Prophet˺
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Have you, O Muhammad (s), received the story of Moses (hadīthu Mūsā operates [the clause that follows]),
verses.romanUrdu: Kya tumhein Moosa ke qissey ki khabar pahunchi hai

verses.uthmani: إِذْ نَادَىٰهُ رَبُّهُۥ بِٱلْوَادِ ٱلْمُقَدَّسِ طُوًى
verses.indopak: اِذۡ نَادٰٮهُ رَبُّهٗ بِالۡوَادِ الۡمُقَدَّسِ طُوًى ۚ
verses.saheeh: When his Lord called to him in the sacred valley of Tuwa,
verses.khattab: His Lord called him in the sacred valley of Ṭuwa
verses.jalalayn: ﻿when his Lord called out to him in the holy valley of Tuwā? — this is the name of the valley (it may be read with nunation, Tuwan, or without) — and He said:
verses.romanUrdu: Jab uske Rubb ne usey Tuwa ke muqaddas wadi(valley) mein pukara tha

verses.saheeh: "Go to Pharaoh. Indeed, he has transgressed.
verses.khattab: ˹commanding,˺ “Go to Pharaoh, for he has truly transgressed ˹all bounds˺
verses.jalalayn: ﻿‘Go to Pharaoh; he has indeed become rebellious, he has exceeded [all] bounds with his disbelief,
verses.romanUrdu: Ke Firaun ke paas ja, woh sarkash ho gaya hai

verses.uthmani: فَقُلْ هَل لَّكَ إِلَىٰٓ أَن تَزَكَّىٰ
verses.indopak: فَقُلۡ هَلۡ لَّكَ اِلٰٓى اَنۡ تَزَكّٰى ۙ
verses.transliteration: faqul hal laka il<u>a</u> an tazakk<u>a</u>
verses.saheeh: And say to him, 'Would you [be willing to] purify yourself
verses.khattab: And say, ‘Would you ˹be willing to˺ purify yourself
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and say, “Would you — I call you [to] — purify yourself (tazakkā: a variant reading has tazzakkā, where the original second tā’ [of tatazakkā] has been assimilated with the zāy), to purge yourself of idolatry, by bearing witness that there is no god but God,
verses.romanUrdu: Aur ussey keh, kya tu iske liye tayyar hai ke pakeezgi ikhtiyar karey

verses.saheeh: And let me guide you to your Lord so you would fear [Him]?'"
verses.khattab: and let me guide you to your Lord so that you will be in awe ˹of Him˺?’”
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and allow me to guide you to your Lord, to show you how to know Him (ma‘rifa) by way of proofs, so that you may have fear [of Him]?” ’
verses.romanUrdu: Aur mai terey Rubb ki taraf teri rehnumai karoon to (uska) khauf terey andar paida ho?”

verses.saheeh: And he showed him the greatest sign,
verses.khattab: Then Moses showed him the great sign
verses.jalalayn: ﻿So he showed him the greatest sign, from among His nine signs, namely, the [glowing] hand or the [slithering] staff.
verses.romanUrdu: Phir Moosa ne (Firaun ke paas ja kar) usko badi nishani dikhai

verses.saheeh: But Pharaoh denied and disobeyed.
verses.khattab: but he denied and disobeyed ˹Allah˺
verses.jalalayn: ﻿But he, Pharaoh, denied, Moses, and disobeyed, God, exalted be He.
verses.romanUrdu: Magar usne jhutla diya aur na mana

verses.saheeh: Then he turned his back, striving.
verses.khattab: then turned his back, striving ˹against the truth˺
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Then he turned his back, to faith, going about in haste, throughout the land causing corruption.
verses.romanUrdu: Phir chaal baaziyan karne ke liye palta

verses.saheeh: And he gathered [his people] and called out
verses.khattab: Then he summoned ˹his people˺ and called out
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Then he gathered, he assembled the sorcerers and his armies, and proclaimed,
verses.romanUrdu: Aur logon ko jama karke usne pukaar kar kaha

verses.saheeh: And said, "I am your most exalted lord."
verses.khattab: saying, “I am your lord, the most high!”
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and said, ‘I am your most high lord!’, above whom is no other lord.
verses.romanUrdu: “Main tumhara sabse bada Rubb hoon”

verses.saheeh: So Allah seized him in exemplary punishment for the last and the first [transgression].
verses.khattab: So Allah overtook him, making him an example in this life and the next
verses.jalalayn: ﻿So God seized him, He destroyed him by drowning him, as punishment for the latter, that is to say, these [last] words [of his], and for the former, that is to say, his saying previously, ‘I do not know of any god for you other than me’ [Q. 28:38] — and between the two [claims made by Pharaoh] was an interval of forty years.
verses.romanUrdu: Aakhir-e-kaar Allah ne usey aakhirat aur duniya ke azaab mei pakad liya

verses.uthmani: إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَعِبْرَةًۭ لِّمَن يَخْشَىٰٓ
verses.indopak: اِنَّ فِىۡ ذٰلِكَ لَعِبۡرَةً لِّمَنۡ يَّخۡشٰى ؕ
verses.saheeh: Indeed in that is a warning for whoever would fear [Allah].
verses.khattab: Surely in this is a lesson for whoever stands in awe of ˹Allah˺
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Assuredly in that, which is mentioned, there is a moral for him who fears, God, exalted be He.
verses.romanUrdu: Dar haqeeqat is mein badi ibrat hai har us shaks ke liye jo darey

verses.uthmani: ءَأَنتُمْ أَشَدُّ خَلْقًا أَمِ ٱلسَّمَآءُ ۚ بَنَىٰهَا
verses.indopak: ءَاَنۡتُمۡ اَشَدُّ خَلۡقًا اَمِ السَّمَآءُ ؕ بَنٰٮهَا
verses.transliteration: aantum ashaddu khalqan ami alssamao banaha
verses.saheeh: Are you a more difficult creation or is the heaven? Allah constructed it.
verses.khattab: Which is harder to create: you or the sky? He built it
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Are you (read a-antum pronouncing both hamzas, or by substituting an alif for the second one, not pronouncing it and inserting an alif between the one not pronounced and the former, or without [this insertion]), namely, [you] the deniers of the Resurrection, harder to create or the heaven which He has built?, harder to create (banāhā: an explication of the manner of [its] creation).
verses.romanUrdu: Kya tum logon ki takhleeq(paidaish) zyada sakht kaam hai ya aasmaan ki? Allah ne usko banaya

verses.saheeh: He raised its ceiling and proportioned it.
verses.khattab: raising it high and forming it flawlessly
verses.jalalayn: ﻿He made it rise high — an explication of the manner of [its] construction; in other words, He made its vertical extension high; it is also said that samkahā means ‘its ceiling’ — and levelled it: He made it even, flawless,
verses.romanUrdu: Uski chhat(ceiling) khoob unchi uthayi phir uska tawazun qayam kiya(proportioned it)

verses.saheeh: And He darkened its night and extracted its brightness.
verses.khattab: He dimmed its night, and brought forth its daylight
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and darkened its night, and brought forth its day: He exposed the light of its sun (‘night’ has been annexed to it [the heaven] because it represents its shade, and likewise the ‘sun’, because it represents its light);
verses.romanUrdu: Aur uski raat dhaanki aur uska din nikala

verses.saheeh: And after that He spread the earth.
verses.khattab: As for the earth, He spread it out as well
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and after that He spread out the earth: He made it flat, for it had been created before the heaven, but without having been spread out;
verses.romanUrdu: Iske baad zameen ko usne bichaya

verses.saheeh: He extracted from it its water and its pasture,
verses.khattab: bringing forth its water and pastures
verses.jalalayn: ﻿from it He has brought forth (akhraja: a circumstantial qualifier with a suppressed [preceding] qad, that is to say, mukhrijan, ‘bringing forth [from it]’) its waters, by making its springs gush forth, and its pastures, what cattle graze, of trees and herbage, and what humans consume of foods and fruits (the use of mar‘ā to express this [of the earth] is figurative),
verses.romanUrdu: Uske andar se uska paani aur chara nikala

verses.saheeh: And the mountains He set firmly
verses.khattab: and setting the mountains firmly ˹upon it˺—
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and has set firm the mountains, on the face of the earth so that it stays still,
verses.romanUrdu: Aur pahad usmein gaadh diye

verses.saheeh: As provision for you and your grazing livestock.
verses.khattab: all as ˹a means of˺ sustenance for you and your animals
verses.jalalayn: ﻿as a [source of] sustenance (an object denoting reason for an implied [verbal clause], in other words, fa‘ala dhālika mut‘atan or tamtī‘an, ‘He did this to provide [a source of] sustenance’) for you and your flocks (an‘ām is the plural of na‘am, which are camels, cows and sheep).
verses.romanUrdu: Saaman-e-zeist(provision) ke taur par tumharay liye aur tumharey maweshion ke liye

verses.saheeh: But when there comes the greatest Overwhelming Calamity -
verses.khattab: But, when the Supreme Disaster comes to pass—
verses.jalalayn: ﻿So when the Greatest Catastrophe befalls — the second blast —
verses.romanUrdu: Phir jab woh hungama-e-azeem barpa hoga

verses.saheeh: The Day when man will remember that for which he strove,
verses.khattab: the Day every person will remember all ˹their˺ striving
verses.jalalayn: ﻿the day when man will remember (yawma yatadhakkaru’l-insānu substitutes for idhā, ‘when’) his efforts, in the [life of the] world, in the way of good or evil,
verses.romanUrdu: Jis roz Insan apna sab kiya dhara yaad karega

verses.saheeh: And Hellfire will be exposed for [all] those who see -
verses.khattab: and the Hellfire will be displayed for all to see—
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and the Hell-fire, the consuming Fire, is revealed for all to see, for every on-looker (the response to idhā, ‘when’, is [what follows]):
verses.romanUrdu: Aur har dekhne wale ke samney dozak khol kar rakh di jayegi

verses.saheeh: So as for he who transgressed
verses.khattab: then as for those who transgressed
verses.jalalayn: ﻿as for him who was rebellious, [who] disbelieved,
verses.romanUrdu: To jisne sarkashi(transgress) ki thi

verses.saheeh: And preferred the life of the world,
verses.khattab: and preferred the ˹fleeting˺ life of this world
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and preferred the life of this world, by pursuing [carnal] desires,
verses.romanUrdu: Aur dunya ki zindagi ko tarjeeh di thi

verses.saheeh: Then indeed, Hellfire will be [his] refuge.
verses.khattab: the Hellfire will certainly be ˹their˺ home
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Hell-fire will indeed be the abode, his abode.
verses.romanUrdu: dozakh hi uska thikana hogi

verses.uthmani: وَأَمَّا مَنْ خَافَ مَقَامَ رَبِّهِۦ وَنَهَى ٱلنَّفْسَ عَنِ ٱلْهَوَىٰ
verses.indopak: وَاَمَّا مَنۡ خَافَ مَقَامَ رَبِّهٖ وَ نَهَى النَّفۡسَ عَنِ الۡهَوٰى ۙ
verses.transliteration: waama man khafa maqama rabbihi wanaha alnnafsa 'ani alhawa
verses.saheeh: But as for he who feared the position of his Lord and prevented the soul from [unlawful] inclination,
verses.khattab: And as for those who were in awe of standing before their Lord and restrained themselves from ˹evil˺ desires
verses.jalalayn: ﻿But as for him who feared the stance before his Lord, his standing before Him, and forbade the, evil-bidding, soul from [pursuing] desire, that leads to perdition as a result of [that person’s] lusting after [carnal] desires,
verses.romanUrdu: Aur jisne apne Rubb ke samney khade honay ka khauf kiya tha aur nafs ko buri khwaishaat se baaz rakha tha

verses.saheeh: Then indeed, Paradise will be [his] refuge.
verses.khattab: Paradise will certainly be ˹their˺ home
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Paradise will indeed be the abode: in sum the response [to idhā, ‘when’, verse 34] is that the disobedient one will be in the Fire and the obedient one in Paradise.
verses.romanUrdu: Jannat uska thikana hogi

verses.saheeh: They ask you, [O Muhammad], about the Hour: when is its arrival?
verses.khattab: They ask you ˹O Prophet˺ regarding the Hour, “When will it be?”
verses.jalalayn: ﻿They, that is, the disbelievers of Mecca, will ask you about the Hour: when will it set in?, when will it come to pass and when will it begin?
verses.romanUrdu: Yeh log tumse puchte hain ke aakhir woh ghadi kab aakar thehre gi

verses.saheeh: In what [position] are you that you should mention it?
verses.khattab: But it is not for you to tell its time
verses.jalalayn: ﻿What have you to do with the mention of it?, in other words, you have no knowledge of it in order to mention it.
verses.romanUrdu: Tumhara kya kaam ke us ka waqt batao

verses.saheeh: To your Lord is its finality.
verses.khattab: That knowledge rests with your Lord ˹alone˺
verses.jalalayn: ﻿With your Lord it belongs ultimately, ultimate knowledge of it [lies with Him]; none other than Him has any knowledge of it.
verses.romanUrdu: Us ka ilm to Allah par khatm hai

verses.saheeh: You are only a warner for those who fear it.
verses.khattab: Your duty is only to warn whoever is in awe of it
verses.jalalayn: ﻿You are only a warner for, your warning will only benefit, the one who fears it.
verses.romanUrdu: Tum sirf khabardar karne waley ho har us shaks ko jo uska khauff karey

verses.uthmani: كَأَنَّهُمْ يَوْمَ يَرَوْنَهَا لَمْ يَلْبَثُوٓا۟ إِلَّا عَشِيَّةً أَوْ ضُحَىٰهَا
verses.indopak: كَاَنَّهُمۡ يَوۡمَ يَرَوۡنَهَا لَمۡ يَلۡبَثُوۡۤا اِلَّا عَشِيَّةً اَوۡ ضُحٰٮهَا
verses.transliteration: kaannahum yawma yarawnah<u>a</u> lam yalbathoo ill<u>a</u> 'ashiyyatan aw <u>d</u>u<u>ha</u>h<u>a</u>
verses.saheeh: It will be, on the Day they see it, as though they had not remained [in the world] except for an afternoon or a morning thereof.
verses.khattab: On the Day they see it, it will be as if they had stayed ˹in the world˺ no more than one evening or its morning
verses.jalalayn: ﻿The day they see it, it will be as if they had only tarried, in their graves, for an evening or the morning thereof, that is to say, [as if only] one evening of a day or its morning (the annexation of duhā, ‘morning’, to ‘ashiyya, ‘evening’, is valid, on the basis of their contiguity, since both constitute either side of the day; the annexation has also allowed for the word to fall in harmony with the end-rhyme of the verses).
verses.romanUrdu: Jis roz yeh log usey dekh lengey to inhein yun mehsoos hoga ke (yeh duniya mein ya halat-e-mout mei) bas ek din ke pichle pehar ya aglay pehar tak thehrey hai
